data.title: Žilina-Zástranie, Straník – a hillfort above the Žilina Basin
data.excerpt: The Straník hillfort lies south-east of Žilina-Zástranie at a spot height of 769 m, its fortified area of about 6.7 ha broken by three or four gateways. Finds of the Lusatian and Púchov cultures show it as the central fortress of the eastern part of the Žilina Basin, even though treasure hunters have long been plundering the site.
data.metaTitle: Straník – a hillfort above the Žilina Basin
data.metaDescription: The Straník hillfort above Žilina-Zástranie at 769 m, surveyed from 1947 by A. Petrovský-Šichman and long a target of treasure hunters and looting.

children.text: The archaeological site of the Straník hillfort lies to the south-east of the village at a spot height of 769 m above sea level. The site was frequently disturbed by treasure hunters in the past as well, and a great many finds have been lost in private collections.

blocks.caption: Fig. 1 Žilina-Zástranie, Straník: a view of the Straník hillfort and the plan of the fortification.
blocks.alt: Fig. 1 Žilina-Zástranie, Straník: a view of the Straník hillfort and the plan of the fortification.

children.text: The first evidence of earlier occupation at the site was brought by the surveys of A. Petrovský-Šichman as early as 1947. He handed most of the finds over to the Archaeological Institute at the Slovak National Museum in Martin, to Professor V. Budinský-Krička, under whom he also studied archaeology and whose assistant he became after completing his studies. The archive of the Institute of Archaeology of the Slovak Academy of Sciences in Nitra holds find report no. 568/51 of 1951 on a trench dug in 1949 in the middle of the rampart, measuring 0.5 x 2.5 m and 0.3–0.8 m deep, down to the level of the bedrock. The sherd material was deposited in the Žilina Museum. A report of 1946 records the find of an early Slavic sherd on the summit of the hillfort (A. Petrovský-Šichman: Slovanské osídlenie severného Slovenska. In: Vlastivedný zborník Považia VI, 1964, p. 73, pl. VII:5). All the other finds from various parts of the hillfort, obtained from surface collection and chance donations, belong mainly to the Lusatian culture of the Late to Final Bronze Age and then above all to the Late Iron Age – the Late La Tène, which in the setting of northern Slovakia is represented by the Púchov culture (Fig. 2). The Straník hillfort commands the territory of the eastern part of the Žilina Basin, where the most fertile soil is also to be found, especially between Teplička and Varín.

The fortified area of the hillfort measures about 450 x 150 m, which is approximately 6.7 ha (Fig. 1). On the northern and western sides the fortification is broken by 3–4 gateways. After the northern rampart was disturbed during the construction of a track for hang-glider pilots, pottery of the Late Bronze Age was found in the body of the rampart, which represents probably the earliest dating of the hillfort's fortification. With its massive ramparts, the hillfort on Straník protected above all the population of the surrounding hamlets, of which there are a fair number in the cadastral areas of the nearest villages. They are attested by archaeological finds from the Neolithic down to the High Middle Ages (Fig. 3). By way of illustration we may mention the settlements at Gbeľany, Teplička and Varín; the urnfield cemeteries at Gbeľany and Varín, or the fortlets at Belá, Dolná Tižina, Terchová and Varín. Mention should also be made of the chance finds of bronze objects, such as the bronze axe from Teplička, found during the construction of a waterworks, the bronze sickle from the settlement at Prostredný lán, the flanged bronze axe of the Early Bronze Age from Terchová (Fig. 3); the iron javelin from Terchová at Medziholie and another from Varín; the 9th-century iron sword from Varín, the iron spearhead from Belá at Vyvieračky, and so on. The intensity of occupation was exceptionally great especially in the period of the Late to Final Bronze Age and in the Late La Tène period. And it was precisely at that time that the hillfort on Straník evidently served as the central fortress of the eastern part of the Žilina Basin, thus helping the main fortification at Divinka on Veľký vrch to organise the life of the society of the time. At Divinka, too, a massive fortification arose at that time, which became the central hillfort not only of the Žilina Basin but also of the Bytča Basin, since it lies precisely on the boundary between them.

children.text: The hillfort on Straník fulfilled its function in at least two chronological horizons – in the Late to Final Bronze Age and then in the Late La Tène period, possibly extending into the earlier part of the Early Roman period. Although no archaeological excavation has been carried out here so far, the quantity of finds collected in the area of the fortification clearly documents its standing in the earliest history of this region, and it may therefore be said that its significance reached beyond the bounds of the region of north-western Slovakia, so that it was rightly included in the list of important monuments of Slovakia. Today it is difficult to examine the original composition of the occupation layers in detail, after the long-lasting looting of the site and the frequent disturbance of the original deposition of the finds. Any intervention in the layers of the hillfort devalues the original find situation and thereby also prevents the scientific evaluation of the finds obtained. Today it is no longer enough merely to collect ever more objects and store them in depositories; the whole complex of the site must be investigated, together with the original deposition of the settlement layers and of the objects within them.
Author of the text: Mgr. Jozef Moravčík
Jozef Moravčík: NIEKTORÉ OPEVNENIA V CENTRÁLNEJ ČASTI ŽILINSKEJ KOTLINY in Hradiská – Svedkovia dávnych čias. Dolná Mariková 2015

In conclusion we bring you a hot piece of news – a hoard of Celtic coins of the Veľký Bysterec type and a gold Boian stater, which was found at the hillfort and which was published in the article Radoslav Čambal – Marek Budaj: Hromadný nález mincí veľkobystereckého typu zo Straníka (okr. Žilina), Múzeum mincí a medailí v Kremnici, 2016
